title: Design System: Pulse — Personal Productivity OS

display.purpose: Greeting line and primary titles that anchor a surface.

shadows.name: float
shadows.purpose: The docked global timer bar and modal dialogs — only elements that float above the page.

motion.name: ease-out-signal
motion.purpose: State transitions: page-in, rise-in, modal, toast, accordion (0.22–0.28s).

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: Colors and borders (100–200ms) on interactive elements.

motion.name: ring-sweep
motion.purpose: Progress ring value sweep; tick bead travels 700ms.

narrative.northStar: The focus cabin in a forest at night
narrative.overview: Pulse is a personal productivity OS for a single user. The interface reads like a quiet, rain-damped cabin office built on paper-dark forest floors: near-black green grounds, hairline borders that catch the light like wood grain, and one bright lime accent — the "signal light" — drawn only where the user acts or earns progress. Premium-minimalist: nothing decorative, everything functional, but with the exactness of instruments rather than the looseness of a toy. The mode is Operate: scanability and consistency outrank expression, so the design depends on precision rather than spectacle — fine-stroked progress rings with a tick at the current value, tabular numerals for metrics, hover-only affordances on desktop that become always-visible on touch, and motion tuned to 100–300ms with a gentle ease-out. The signature is the progress ring: fine stroke, muted green track, lime sweep, and a small tick bead that travels the rim to the live value. Color is scarce and rationed; the lime accent sits on polished, reflective rounded surfaces, has no gradient around it, and never decorates idle chrome.
keyCharacteristics: Rationed lime on dark forest ground — accent means "act here" or "progress earned"
Fine-stroked progress rings with a traveling tick bead as the signature element
Hairline borders, soft cards, generous rounded corners (14–22px)
Tabular numerals on every metric; Inter throughout
100–300ms eased-in-out motion that collapses under reduced motion
Hover-revealed desktop affordances; always-visible on touch

rules.name: The Rationed Signal Rule
rules.body: The lime accent is used on ≤10% of any given screen. It marks action and earned progress — never idle chrome, never as a wash. Rarity is the point.

rules.name: The No-Glow Rule
rules.body: Accents never glow, blur, or emit. The ring's fine stroke and tick speak louder than any halo.

rules.name: The Rationed Boldness Rule
rules.body: Bold (700) is reserved for the value the eye must land on — the greeting, the ring value, section titles, the active metric.

rules.name: The Tabular-Precision Rule
rules.body: Every live metric renders with tabular-nums. Numbers that change must not reflow the layout as they tick.

rules.name: The Flat-by-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. Shadows appear only for elements that physically float above the page (timer bar, modal).

dos: Do draw the lime accent only where the user acts or progress is earned — keep it under ~10% of the screen.
Do use the progress ring for "how far toward done" and tabular numerals for any live metric.
Do keep cards flat in the page flow; reserve shadows for the floating timer bar and modals.
Do use Hairline (1px) borders and tonal elevation (Surface → Elevated → Soft) to separate layers.
Do keep all UI on Inter; bold only the value or title the eye must land on.
Do collapse every animation under prefers-reduced-motion — reveal the same data instantly.
donts: Don't apply gradients, glows, or backdrop blurs to the accent or cards — flat instrument precision only.
Don't use the lime as a wash or background for reading surfaces; it is an action/earned color.
Don't race every second of a timer through a global re-render; only the consuming views tick.
Don't hide a hover-only affordance on touch; reveal it always at small screens.
Don't stack weights — hierarchy comes from size/tracking/color, not bolding everything.
